name: CLIPSeg (text-prompted segmentation, CLIP B/16)
plain: CLIPSeg (Lüddecke and Ecker, CVPR 2022): one coarse mask for whatever a free-text prompt names, from a frozen CLIP ViT-B/16 and a small decoder. Apache-2.0 code and weights; the PhraseCut training data has no stated terms.
summary: CLIPSeg (Lüddecke and Ecker 2022): a frozen CLIP ViT-B/16 with a small transformer decoder that segments whatever a free-text prompt names; the text embedding conditions the decoder by FiLM. Semantic: one mask per prompt (all pixels of the concept), at 352 x 352, resized to the image. Pass `text=` at call time. The portable `module()` is the network on the normalised 352 x 352 image plus a projected text embedding.

papers.title: Image Segmentation Using Text and Image Prompts

official.reason: fastforks follows the transformers port, which loads the authors' converted weights (CIDAS/clipseg-rd64-refined) without the repo's CLIP dependency.

limitations: No accuracy measurement: CLIPSeg is scored on PhraseCut and Pascal-5i one-shot splits, which are not part of the evaluation data here; tiers are compared by output parity and speed only.
Requires the optional transformers library (the network is its `CLIPSegForImageSegmentation`).
The original in the benchmarks and goldens is the Hugging Face transformers 5.19.0 port with the authors' weights (CIDAS/clipseg-rd64-refined); the authors' timojl/clipseg code was not run.

Text prompts only (no box exemplars or visual prompts); one instance per prompt: its mask is every pixel above probability 0.5, its score the highest pixel probability, its box the mask's bounding box.
The image is resized to 352 x 352 without keeping the aspect ratio, as the original processor; masks are coarse (22 x 22 patch tokens).
task_io: Input: one image plus a point, box or text prompt. Output: masks with quality scores.

variants.name: clipseg

training_data.name: PhraseCut (referring-phrase masks on Visual Genome images)

licence.training_note: The decoder is trained on PhraseCut (extended with visual prompts in the paper; the refined rd64 checkpoint, reduce_dim 64); the CLIP towers are OpenAI's frozen ViT-B/16, trained on web image-text pairs that were not released (CLIPSeg paper, arXiv:2112.10003).

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 1, resized inside to the fixed encoder input 352x352 (the default export size)

quality.title: COCO val2017, every 10th image, class masks, class / prompt mIoU %
quality.protocol: One text prompt per present COCO class. The label is the union of the class's non-crowd masks. Scores average pixel IoU aggregated per class, and IoU per image and prompt.

portable.note: One prompt per present class. IoU against the union of same-class instance masks. Stage boundaries vary by mode.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.0005 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.1 and p99 <= 0.5 (absolute error of the output `boxes`).
